items.title: Participants in the Youth skills Enterprise Initiative Program, Zambia

items.sentence_raw: Although small-scale business training and credit programs have become more common throughout the world, relatively little attention has been paid to the need to direct such opportunities to young people.
Even less attention has been paid to children living on the street or in difficult circumstance.
Over the past nine years, Street Kids International (S.K.I.) has been working with partner organizations in Africa, Latin America and India to support the economic lives of street children.
items.explain: Q2: The passage says S.K.I. works to *'support the economic lives of street children'* and helps them *'start their own small business through business training, life skills training and access to credit'*. This directly matches **give business training and loans to street children**. The answer is **D**.

items.sentence_raw: The purpose of this paper is to share some of the lessons S.K.I. and our partners have learned.

Typically, children do not end up on the streets due to a single cause, but to a combination of factors: a dearth of adequately funded schools, the demand for income at home, family breakdown and violence.
items.explain: Q3: The passage lists reasons children end up on streets, including *'the demand for income at home'* — **'demand for income'** means the family needs money, which is **poverty**. ***Don't confuse 'crime' in the list*** — crime is a danger on the street, not a cause of leaving home. The answer is **C**.

items.sentence_raw: The street may be attractive to children as a place to find adventurous play and money.
However, it is also a place where some children are exposed, with little or no protection, to exploitative employment, urban crime, and abuse.

Children who work on the streets are generally involved in unskilled, labor-intensive tasks which require long hours, such as shining shoes, carrying goods, guarding or washing cars, and informal trading.
Some may also earn income through begging, or through theft and other illegal activities.
At the same time, there are street children who take pride in supporting themselves and their families and who often enjoy their work.

Many children may choose entrepreneurship because it allows them a degree of independence, is less exploitative than many forms of paid-employment, and is flexible enough to allow them to participate in other activities such as education and domestic task.
items.explain: Q4: The passage says children choose *'entrepreneurship because it allows them a degree of independence'* — **'entrepreneurship'** means starting your own business. So to become more independent, they **set up their own businesses**. The answer is **C**.

items.sentence_raw: S.K.I. has worked with partner organizations in Latin America, Africa and India to develop innovative opportunities for street children to earn income.
The S.K.I. Bicycle Courier Service first started in the Sudan.
items.explain: Q5: The passage says the courier service *'first started in the Sudan'* and *'A similar program was taken up in Bangalore, India'*. So the two countries are **Sudan** and **India**.

items.sentence_raw: Participants in this enterprise were supplied with bicycles, which they used to deliver parcels and messages, and which they were required to pay for gradually from their wages.
items.explain: Q6: The passage says participants *'were supplied with bicycles'* for the courier service. So the support provided was the provision of **bicycles**.

items.sentence_raw: A similar program was taken up in Bangalore, India.
items.explain: Q5: The passage says the courier service *'first started in the Sudan'* and *'A similar program was taken up in Bangalore, India'*. So the two countries are **Sudan** and **India**.

items.sentence_raw: Another successful project, The Shoe Shine Collective, was a partnership program with the Y.W.C.A. in the Dominican Republic.
items.explain: Q7: The passage names the project in the Dominican Republic as *'The Shoe Shine Collective'*. So the type of project is **Shoe Shine Collective**.

items.sentence_raw: In this project, participants were lent money to purchase shoe shine boxes.
They were also given a safe place to store their equipment, and facilities for individual savings plans.

The Youth Skills Enterprise Initiative in Zambia is a joint program with the Red Cross Society and the Y.W.C.A. Street youths are supported to start their own small business through business training, life skills training and access to credit.
items.explain:
Q2: The passage says S.K.I. works to *'support the economic lives of street children'* and helps them *'start their own small business through business training, life skills training and access to credit'*. This directly matches **give business training and loans to street children**. The answer is **D**.

Q8: The passage says the Zambia program includes *'business training, life skills training and access to credit'*. The table already has 'business training' and 'access to credit', so the missing support is **life skills** training.

items.sentence_raw: The following lessons have emerged from the programs that S.K.I. and partner organizations have created.
Being an entrepreneur is not for everyone, nor for every street child.
items.explain: Q9: The passage directly says *'Being an entrepreneur is not for everyone, nor for every street child'* — this means not any child can do it, even with support. The statement says the opposite, so the answer is **NO**.

items.sentence_raw: Ideally, potential participants will have been involved in the organization's programs for at least six months, and trust and relationship building will have already been established.
The involvement of the participants has been essential to the development of relevant programs.
When children have had a major role in determining procedures, they are more likely to abide by and enforce them.
It is critical for all loans to be linked to training programs that include the development of basic business and life skills.
There are tremendous advantages to involving parents or guardians in the program, where such relationships exist.
Home visits allow staff the opportunity to know where the participants live, and to understand more about each individual's situation.
Small loans are provided initially for purchasing fixed assets such as bicycles, shoe shine kits and basic building materials for a market stall.
As the entrepreneurs gain experience, the enterprises can be gradually expanded and consideration can be given to increasing loan amounts.
items.explain: Q11: The passage says *'consideration can be given to increasing loan amounts'* as entrepreneurs grow — this means more than one loan is possible. The statement says **only one fixed loan**, which contradicts this. So the answer is **NO**.

items.sentence_raw: The loan amount in S.K.I. programs have generally ranged from US$30 - $100.
All S.K.I. programs have charged interest on the loans, primarily to get the entrepreneurs used to the concept of paying interest on borrowed money.
items.explain: Q12: The passage says all programs *'have charged interest on the loans'* — **'interest'** means extra money you pay back. So children do pay back **slightly more money than they borrowed**. The answer is **YES**.

items.sentence_raw: Generally the rates have been modest (lower than bank rates.)
There is a need to recognize the importance of access to credit for impoverished young people seeking to fulfill economic needs.
The provision of small loans to support the entrepreneurial dreams and ambitions of youth can be an effective means to help them change their lives.
However, we believe that credit must be extended in association with other types of support that help participants develop critical life skills as well as productive businesses.
items.explain: Q13: The conclusion says credit *'must be extended in association with other types of support'* — **'in association with'** means as part of a bigger package. This matches **as part of a wider program of aid**. The answer is **A**.

orphan_explain_map.10: Q10: The passage talks about involving parents and home visits, but it never mentions giving **financial support** to families. ***The passage says nothing about money for families*** — it neither confirms nor denies this. So the answer is **NOT GIVEN**.
